nodes.text: Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Perform rare-disease whole-exome sequencing analysis: align or use supplied WES alignments, call and annotate germline variants, apply quality filtering, and prioritize candidate diagnostic variants. | germline rare-disease variant analysis from whole-exome sequencing reads or aligned exome data, including variant calling, annotation, inheritance-aware filtering where available, and diagnostic variant prioritization → annotated prioritized VCF and candidate-variant report

Perform RNA-seq rare-disease analysis to detect aberrant gene expression and splicing events relevant to molecular diagnosis. | rare-disease RNA-seq analysis from raw reads or expression/splicing-ready RNA-seq data, including quality control, alignment or quantification, outlier expression detection, and aberrant splicing detection → gene-expression and splice-outlier report

Integrate WES candidate variants with RNA-seq expression and splicing outliers to prioritize a molecular diagnosis for rare disease. | integration of annotated germline exome variants with RNA-seq expression and splicing outliers for rare-disease diagnosis → ranked candidate genes, variants, supporting transcriptomic evidence, and diagnostic report

Analyze my WES data for a complete rare disease workup, including variant calling or processing, annotation, and candidate prioritization. | Rare-disease exome variant analysis from user-provided WES data, with input format and variant-calling scope to be confirmed → annotated, prioritized candidate variants.

Analyze my RNA-seq data for a complete rare disease workup, including evidence of abnormal expression or splicing where appropriate. | Rare-disease RNA-seq analysis with assay type and input format to be confirmed → expression and splicing evidence for candidate genes.

Integrate my WES and RNA-seq findings for a complete rare disease workup and prioritize candidate diagnoses using available phenotype and inheritance information. | Integrate exome variant annotations with RNA expression and splicing evidence and available phenotype information → prioritized candidate variants and genes for rare-disease interpretation.

Quantify transcript abundance from RNA-seq reads using Salmon for differential transcript usage analysis. | transcript-level quantification from bulk RNA-seq FASTQ reads using Salmon → transcript-level abundance and count estimates

Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport and prepare transcript/exon-level count data for DEXSeq differential transcript usage testing. | import transcript-level Salmon quantifications with tximport and construct DEXSeq-compatible count and annotation objects → normalized feature-level count data for DTU testing

Run DEXSeq differential transcript usage testing and stageR stage-wise FDR control on imported RNA-seq transcript quantifications. | differential transcript usage testing with DEXSeq followed by stageR stage-wise false-discovery-rate control → gene-level and transcript-level DTU results with adjusted p-values

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

Quantify RNA-seq transcripts with Salmon for the rnaseqDTU-style workflow. | Transcript-level RNA-seq quantification with Salmon from sequencing reads and a transcriptome reference → transcript abundance and estimated counts.

Import Salmon transcript quantifications with tximport for differential transcript usage analysis. | Import Salmon transcript abundance and estimated counts with tximport → transcript-level data suitable for differential transcript usage testing.

Test differential transcript usage with DEXSeq using the imported transcript data. | DEXSeq differential transcript usage testing on imported transcript-level RNA-seq estimates and sample metadata → transcript-level test statistics and p-values.

Apply stageR to the differential transcript usage results for stage-wise FDR control. | Stage-wise multiple testing with stageR using gene-level screening and transcript-level confirmation p-values → FDR-controlled differential transcript usage results.

Reproduce the Replogle et al. (2022) Perturb-seq guide-assignment stage: assign CRISPR guide identities to single cells from Perturb-seq sequencing data, producing a cell-by-guide assignment matrix with assignment QC. | Perturb-seq CRISPR guide assignment from single-cell sequencing / feature-barcode data → per-cell guide identities, guide UMI counts, multiplet/low-confidence assignment flags, and cell-by-guide matrix

Perform Perturb-seq CRISPR screen hit calling using guide-assigned single-cell expression profiles to identify gene perturbations with significant transcriptional effects. | single-cell CRISPR Perturb-seq hit calling from guide-assigned expression data → statistically significant perturbation effects, gene-level hit scores, effect sizes, and multiple-testing-adjusted p-values

Model Perturb-seq transcriptional perturbation states and generate a latent embedding using scVI/scANVI, integrating guide assignments and hit-calling results to visualize and annotate perturbation-response states. | scVI/scANVI latent-variable modeling of guide-assigned Perturb-seq single-cell expression data → batch-corrected latent embedding, perturbation-state clusters, cell-state annotations, and UMAP visualization

Identify and characterize tumor-reactive T-cell populations from scRNA-seq data, including T-cell clustering, phenotype/state annotation, exhaustion/activation markers, and potential TCR clonotype expansion where available. | single-cell RNA-seq T-cell subset analysis and tumor-reactive T-cell state identification from processed scRNA-seq data or raw reads → annotated T-cell clusters, tumor-reactivity scores, marker genes, and clonotype-associated populations when V(D)J data are available

Predict patient-specific tumor neoantigens from tumor somatic variants using HLA typing and peptide–MHC binding prediction, prioritizing candidate immunogenic mutant peptides. | tumor neoantigen prediction from somatic tumor variants with patient HLA alleles and optional tumor RNA expression evidence → ranked mutant peptide–MHC candidate neoantigens

Assign CRISPR guides to cells for an end-to-end Perturb-seq screen analysis, using Replogle et al. 2022 as a methodological reference. | Assign guide identities to single cells from Perturb-seq guide-capture data → cell-level guide assignments and assignment quality metrics.

Call significant CRISPR perturbation hits from the Perturb-seq screen using the assigned guides and gene-expression data, guided by Replogle et al. 2022. | Statistical hit calling in a Perturb-seq CRISPR screen using single-cell expression and cell-level guide assignments → perturbation effects, significance estimates and ranked hits.

Analyze perturbation states with scVI/scANVI embeddings after guide assignment and hit calling, using Replogle et al. 2022 as a methodological reference. | Model single-cell perturbation states using scVI/scANVI embeddings of expression data with guide assignments and hit annotations → latent embeddings and perturbation-state summaries.

Identify tumor-reactive T cells in the user's scRNA-seq data. | Single-cell RNA-seq analysis to identify and characterize tumor-reactive T-cell populations using expression signatures and cell annotation → candidate cells and supporting markers

Predict tumor neoantigens; obtain the necessary variant and HLA inputs from the user. | Tumor neoantigen prediction using somatic variant calls and patient HLA alleles → candidate mutant peptides and predicted HLA binding

Run graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference with R Monocle3 on a single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using an optional cluster and root-cell specification; export annotated AnnData, pseudotime tables, and trajectory plots. | graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference on processed single-cell AnnData (.h5ad) using Monocle3 → cell-level pseudotime annotations, trajectory graph, CSV results, annotated h5ad, and PNG visualizations

Run RNA velocity analysis with Python scVelo on the same single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using the requested velocity mode; export velocity-annotated AnnData, per-cell CSV results, and velocity visualizations. | RNA velocity estimation on processed single-cell AnnData (.h5ad) using scVelo, with selectable velocity mode → velocity-annotated h5ad, cell-level CSV results, and PNG stream/embedding plots

Load Illumina EPIC/450K methylation-array IDAT files with minfi and perform quality control plus functional normalization; alternatively ingest Bismark bisulfite coverage produced by nf-core/methylseq. | Illumina EPIC/450K DNA methylation-array preprocessing from raw IDAT files using minfi (sample/QC assessment and functional normalization) → normalized methylation values and QC report; alternatively prepare Bismark bisulfite coverage for downstream differential methylation

Perform DSS-based differential methylation analysis on normalized EPIC/450K methylation values or Bismark bisulfite coverage to identify differentially methylated CpGs and regions. | DSS differential methylation testing from normalized DNA methylation-array values or Bismark bisulfite coverage → differentially methylated CpG sites and regions with effect sizes and multiple-testing-adjusted p-values

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment analysis on DSS differential-methylation results, accounting for array probe-to-gene representation bias. | gene-set and pathway enrichment on differential DNA methylation results using missMethyl, with correction for CpG probe/gene representation bias → enriched GO terms and pathways
Run RNA-seq analysis and differential expression

Build the Monocle3 graph-based pseudotime subworkflow for the shared single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using monocle_cluster and root_cell as parameters. The overall specification also lists CSV input and AnnData, CSV, h5ad, and PNG outputs. | Graph-based single-cell trajectory inference and pseudotime with R Monocle3 from AnnData h5ad input, with optional CSV input as specified → trajectory annotations and visualizations.

Build the scVelo RNA velocity subworkflow for the shared single-cell AnnData h5ad input, using velocity_mode as a parameter. The overall specification also lists CSV input and AnnData, CSV, h5ad, and PNG outputs. | Single-cell RNA velocity inference with Python scVelo from AnnData h5ad input, with optional CSV input as specified → velocity annotations and visualizations.
Run RNA-seq analysis and differential expression
predict CYP450 inhibition and hepatic clearance for new chemical entity
predict CYP450 inhibition and hepatic clearance for new chemical entity

Load EPIC or 450K methylation-array IDAT files with minfi and perform functional normalization. | Load Illumina methylation-array IDAT files with minfi and apply functional normalization → normalized methylation measurements.

Use DSS for differential methylation analysis of the normalized EPIC or 450K array data; the wrapper is also applicable to Bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq. | DSS differential methylation analysis on normalized methylation-array measurements, with support for Bismark bisulfite coverage as an alternative input → differential methylation results.

Perform missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differential methylation results. | Gene-set enrichment with missMethyl using differential methylation results and appropriate array probe annotations → enriched gene sets.

Nanostring GeoMx DSP Analysis (GeoMxWorkflows). Bioc Workflow `GeoMxWorkflows` analog: read Nanostring GeoMx DSP NanoStringGeoMxSet, segment-level QC, Q3 normalization, mixed-model linear DE across regions of interest.

Nanostring GeoMx DSP Analysis (GeoMxWorkflows). Bioc Workflow `GeoMxWorkflows` analog: read Nanostring GeoMx DSP NanoStringGeoMxSet, segment-level QC, Q3 normalization, mixed-model linear DE across regions of interest.

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).
FDA Phase II to Phase III dose justification brief

Estimate human pharmacokinetic parameters from rat, mouse, or dog preclinical PK data using interspecies allometric scaling for first-in-human projection. | interspecies allometric scaling of preclinical animal pharmacokinetic parameters (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) to predict human PK parameters and first-in-human dose inputs

Run a mechanistic human PBPK simulation using scaled human PK parameters, with compartmental physiology and organ-specific clearance; optionally model renal or hepatic impairment for special-population dose adjustment. | mechanistic whole-body human PBPK simulation using compound and scaled PK parameters, organ-specific distribution and clearance, with optional renal- or hepatic-impairment submodels → concentration-time profiles and special-population dose-adjustment projections

Perform Monte Carlo simulation on the human PBPK model to characterize interindividual pharmacokinetic variability and exposure distributions. | Monte Carlo population simulation of a parameterized human PBPK model → interindividual concentration-time variability, exposure distributions, and population-level PK summary statistics

Public RNA-seq Reanalysis (recountWorkflow). Bioc Workflow `recountWorkflow` analog: pull uniformly-processed counts from recount2/3 for a study (e.g., SRP), scale counts by read length, run DESeq2 DE with technical replicate handling.

Estimate human pharmacokinetic parameters from rat, mouse, or dog preclinical data for first-in-human dose projection. | Interspecies allometric scaling of preclinical animal pharmacokinetic parameters → estimated human clearance and distribution parameters with scaling diagnostics.

Run a mechanistic human PBPK simulation with organ-specific clearance, optionally including renal or hepatic impairment for special-population dosing. | Mechanistic compartmental PBPK simulation using scaled PK parameters and compound-specific physiological and clearance inputs, optionally including renal or hepatic impairment → human concentration-time profiles and exposure metrics.

Use Monte Carlo sampling to characterize variability in the human PBPK simulation and any selected special populations. | Monte Carlo sampling of PBPK model parameters and population variability → distributions of concentration-time profiles and exposure metrics.

Process RNA-seq data and identify a differential transcriptional signature for the comparison of interest. | bulk RNA-seq processing and differential gene-expression analysis from raw reads or a gene-count matrix → ranked gene signature with log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values

Use the RNA-seq-derived transcriptional signature to find drugs with matching or reversing transcriptional signatures, prioritizing candidate mechanisms and compounds. | signature-based drug repurposing using a ranked differential-expression signature and drug perturbation transcriptomic reference data → connectivity scores, candidate drugs, and mechanisms of action

Public RNA-seq Reanalysis (recountWorkflow). Bioc Workflow `recountWorkflow` analog: pull uniformly-processed counts from recount2/3 for a study (e.g., SRP), scale counts by read length, run DESeq2 DE with technical replicate handling.

Analyze the RNA-seq data to produce a transcriptional signature for drug matching. | RNA-seq expression analysis from an unspecified input format and assay type, producing a gene expression signature for downstream drug matching.

Find drugs with transcriptional signatures matching the RNA-seq-derived signature. | Compare an RNA-seq-derived gene expression signature against drug perturbation transcriptional signatures, such as LINCS, and rank matching compounds.

ICH S7A core battery safety pharmacology panel simulation. Split into 4 phases for BioMate UI phase cards: Phase A: Phase B: Phase C: Phase D:

Validate a NONMEM-format population pharmacokinetic dataset before model execution, checking required fields such as ID, TIME, and DV. | validate a tabular population pharmacokinetic NONMEM-ready dataset for required columns, numeric consistency, missing values, dosing/observation record structure, and time ordering → QC report and validated analysis dataset

Generate a NONMEM control stream for PopPK estimation from the validated dataset. | generate a NONMEM population pharmacokinetic model control stream using a validated tabular dataset → executable NMTRAN control file defining data input, structural model, variability model, residual error model, and estimation settings

Estimate a population pharmacokinetic model using NONMEM nmfe75/nmfe74 when NONMEM_HOME and NONMEM_LICENSE_FILE are available; otherwise automatically execute an equivalent nlmixr2 R model. | fit a nonlinear mixed-effects population pharmacokinetic model from a validated concentration-time dataset and model specification, prioritizing licensed NONMEM execution with automatic nlmixr2 fallback → parameter estimates, random-effects estimates, diagnostics, and model-fit outputs

Phase A: prepare the test compound and define the ICH S7A safety pharmacology simulation inputs, including molecular structure standardization and planned exposure assumptions. | compound structure preparation and safety-pharmacology simulation setup from molecular input → standardized compound representation, exposure assumptions, and analysis-ready inputs

Phase B: simulate ICH S7A cardiovascular safety risks, including ion-channel/hERG-related liability and cardiac electrophysiology risk assessment. | computational cardiovascular safety pharmacology assessment from standardized molecular input → hERG/ion-channel liability, QT/proarrhythmic risk indicators, and cardiovascular safety summary

Phase C: simulate ICH S7A central nervous system and respiratory safety pharmacology risks for the prepared compound. | computational CNS and respiratory safety pharmacology assessment from standardized molecular input → CNS off-target/neurobehavioral risk indicators and respiratory-depression risk indicators

Phase D: integrate cardiovascular, CNS, and respiratory safety simulation results into an ICH S7A core-battery risk assessment and decision-ready report. | integration of cardiovascular, CNS, and respiratory safety pharmacology simulation outputs → endpoint risk ranking, exposure-margin interpretation, alerts, and ICH S7A-style safety summary report

Validate the NONMEM-format population pharmacokinetic dataset, including ID, TIME, DV and other required fields. | Validate a NONMEM-format population pharmacokinetic dataset for required columns and structural consistency → validation report and validated dataset.

Generate a NONMEM control stream for the validated PopPK dataset; the user's step description is truncated. | Generate a NONMEM control stream from a validated pharmacokinetic dataset and specified population PK model → executable control stream.

Estimate population pharmacokinetics with NONMEM nmfe75/nmfe74 when NONMEM_HOME and NONMEM_LICENSE_FILE are set; otherwise use an nlmixr2 R fallback. | Fit a population pharmacokinetic model to a validated NONMEM-format dataset using licensed NONMEM execution or an equivalent nlmixr2 R model as fallback → parameter estimates and fit diagnostics.

Validate a SMILES input file containing one SMILES string and compound ID per line for matched molecular pair analysis. | SMILES-file validation and standardization for a compound library (one SMILES plus identifier per record) → validated, canonicalized molecular table with invalid structures reported

Perform RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated compounds into scaffold cores and R-group fragments. | RDKit RECAP molecular fragmentation of a validated SMILES library → scaffold cores, attachment points, and R-group fragment assignments per compound

Use mmpdb to identify matched molecular pairs and calculate property deltas associated with fragment swaps. | matched molecular pair analysis using mmpdb on a decomposed compound library → fragment substitutions, transformation frequencies, and associated molecular-property deltas

Rank novel scaffolds using transformation frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA) score. | multi-criteria ranking of candidate molecular scaffolds from matched-pair transformations using occurrence frequency, drug-likeness descriptors, and synthetic-accessibility score → prioritized scaffold table

Validate an expression matrix and matched clinical metadata before limma-voom differential-expression and GSVA/ssGSEA pathway analysis. | quality-control and validation of a bulk gene-expression count matrix with matched sample clinical metadata → validated matrix, sample-metadata concordance report, and analysis-ready covariate design

Perform covariate-adjusted differential expression using voom transformation, limma linear modeling, empirical-Bayes moderation, and topTable results including logFC and adjusted P values. | covariate-adjusted differential gene expression on a bulk RNA-seq count matrix using limma-voom linear modeling and eBayes moderation → per-gene log2 fold change, adjusted p-value, and ranked topTable output

Score samples using GSVA/ssGSEA against the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets and identify top pathways enriched in each group. | GSVA and single-sample GSEA scoring of a normalized bulk gene-expression matrix using the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, followed by group-level pathway enrichment comparison → sample signature scores and top enriched pathways per group

Validate a SMILES input file containing one SMILES and compound ID per line. | Validate a molecular input file with one SMILES and identifier per line → valid standardized molecular records and a validation report.

Apply RDKit RECAP decomposition to the validated molecules to obtain scaffolds and R-groups. | Decompose validated SMILES molecules with RDKit RECAP → molecular fragments for scaffold and R-group analysis.

Use mmpdb to identify matched molecular pairs and calculate property deltas for fragment swaps. | Identify matched molecular pairs using mmpdb from molecular records and associated property values → fragment transformations and property deltas.

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness and synthetic accessibility score. | Rank molecular scaffolds using occurrence frequency, drug-likeness and synthetic accessibility scores → ranked scaffold table with component scores.

Validate the expression matrix and clinical metadata for the discovery analysis, including sample matching and required group and covariate fields. | Validate an expression matrix and clinical metadata table for sample correspondence, missing values, and analysis readiness → validated inputs and QC report.

Apply voom and fit a limma linear model with clinical covariates; use eBayes and topTable to report logFC and adjusted P-values. | Differential gene expression using voom transformation of suitable expression counts and a limma linear model with covariates, eBayes and topTable → normalized expression and per-gene log fold changes and adjusted P-values.

Score the 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets using GSVA or ssGSEA and report the top enriched pathways per group. | Gene-set activity scoring on normalized expression using GSVA or ssGSEA and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets → per-sample pathway scores and top pathways by group.
